- Confirm whether the Dedicated pool can be reserved for Q2 ramp (we'll need predictable throughput).

John — thanks for the quick note and great questions. Attached is MAP v3 (Acme_MAP_v3.xlsx) which includes milestones, owners, dependencies, and target dates. High level answers inline below and in the MAP: 

- SSO / KMS ownership: Integration work will be joint — Acme owns inbound SSO configuration and Redwood will provide the KMS/HSM integration and guidance. We list technical owners on the MAP.
- Dedicated pool: We can reserve a Dedicated capacity block for your Q2 ramp. I'll surface sizing options in the MAP and flag an option for an initial reserve + burst.
- Pilot success criteria: added a short success criteria checklist (latency P95 < 400ms for 95k tokens/day, 99.9% uptime during test window, model-quality thresholds on the eval set).

Next steps (proposed):
1) Review MAP v3 and confirm owners by 03/03
2) Procurement to accept SOW and DocuSign by 03/06
3) Engineering kickoff (networking + SSO) week of 03/09
4) Pilot go-live target: 03/18

I've attached the MAP and a draft SOW for procurement to start. Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the milestones.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

We reviewed MAP v3 with our engineering and procurement teams. Thanks for incorporating the criteria and escalation path. Procurement has two small asks before they can route SOW to legal:

2) Need the redline-friendly SOW PDF (they prefer a version without tracked changes and with numbered sections).

Assuming we get those, procurement is good to move the DocuSign flow the week of 03/09. Engineering confirmed they'd be ready for the kickoff the week of 03/09. We're comfortable with the pilot success criteria and the 03/18 pilot go-live target.

- Committed baseline: 1 x p4d-equivalent reserved node (estimate: ~1,200 GPU hours/month). Details and burst policy are in the updated SOW.
- Redline-friendly SOW: attached SOW_Acme_20260304.pdf (clean, numbered sections).
- DocuSign readiness: I've uploaded the final SOW to DocuSign and included the link below; legal can add standard redlines. Procurement contacts should receive the invite after we confirm signatures.

Pilot success criteria (final, per MAP v3):
- Latency: P95 < 400ms on typical production prompt set (validation via Redwood test harness)
- Availability: 99.9% during pilot window (monitoring via Redwood Console)
- Quality: Model eval metrics meet thresholds on our shared eval set (AUC and ROUGE baselines attached in MAP).

Next steps after sign-off call:
1) Procurement completes DocuSign by 03/06
2) Engineering kickoff (networking + SSO + KMS) week of 03/09
3) Capacity validation run: 03/11-03/12
4) Pilot go-live: 03/18

I'll be on the 10am call to confirm signatures and ownership. Vivek and Marissa will be on the call for technical/CS coverage.
